name: Leonie Fairbairn
languages: French (from a convent school in Baltimore, which taught her the rest of her trade by accident)
equipment: A dark green silk dress for the faro table, a black wool travelling dress for everything else, a fur-lined cloak and a pair of good boots she paid $30 for in Salt Lake City
Pocket revolver (Smith & Wesson, .32 rimfire, a six-shot cylinder loaded with five), in a pocket sewn into the cloak
Boot knife in her right boot
A faro layout of enamelled cards on green baize, a dealing box with a mirror she does not use in the Union Saloon, and a case-keeper's abacus
Playing cards, two decks, and a marked deck she keeps for teaching
Mordecai Pottinger's IOUs, $1,100 in all, in his own hand, won at her bank since September
A folded card that was pushed under the door of her room at Moira Kehoe's boarding house on the night of 18 November (if the GM chooses: see vg-scenario-001)
A pocket watch on a chain, a hand mirror, a bottle of laudanum for headaches she does not touch
features: Book Learning (Back East origin: advantage on Investigation to read documents, deeds, ledgers and forged papers; once per long rest she recalls a useful fact about law, process, science or history without a check)

Read the Table (Gambler: proficiency doubled for Gambling and Insight; once per short or long rest, after a minute of watching or talking to a person, she learns one thing they are hiding: a lie, a weapon, the card they need, who they fear or what they want from her)

Ace in the Hole (Gambler: once per turn, extra 2d6 damage to one creature she hits with a finesse Melee weapon or a Sidearm if she has advantage, if another enemy of the target is within 5 ft of it, or if it believed a bluff or lie she told it within the last minute; not part of the damage on her sheet)

Lady Luck (Gambler, 2nd level: 3 luck points, her CHA modifier, regained on a long rest; spend one to roll an extra d20 on an attack, check or save, or to make a creature within 30 ft reroll an attack against her)

Sleeve Gun (Gambler, 2nd level: she draws a concealable weapon as a bonus action unnoticed by anyone not watching her hands, and has advantage on Sleight of Hand to carry one past a search; a bonus action each turn to Dash, Disengage or Hide)

Game: Faro Dealer (Gambler, 3rd level: she runs a faro bank in the Union Saloon and earns 1d6 x 5 dollars a night; the house always knows who is winning, who is drinking and who is broke, and so does she)

Know the Games (Card Sharp background: in any camp she finds the best game, the crooked one and the man who runs both within an hour; she knows the house rules and house cheats of faro, poker and monte, and when to leave town)

personality.traits: I am charming when I choose to be, which is most of the time, and cold when I choose to be, which is when it matters. I never raise my voice. I remember every bet anyone has ever made at my table.
personality.ideals: An honest game is the only honest thing in a mining camp. Everyone at my table knows the odds. Nobody on that list was told theirs.
personality.bonds: My bank: forty dollars' worth of baize and enamel that has paid for my independence for nine years. Moira Kehoe, who let me a room when the hotel would not. And myself, first, always; I am the only person who has ever looked after me.
personality.flaws: I hold grudges like markers and I collect on them. Mordecai Pottinger owes me eleven hundred dollars and sits on the committee, and I want both of those facts to be his problem, not mine, and I may be reckless about how.

appearance: A small, straight-backed woman of thirty-two with dark auburn hair pinned up severely, a pale, composed face, very fine hands and a low, amused voice. At the table she wears green silk and no jewellery; off it, black wool and a cloak, and nobody remembers her unless she wants them to.
backstory: Leonie Fairbairn was born in Baltimore in 1832, the daughter of a dancing master who drank and a mother who kept the family on her needle, and was educated by nuns on a scholarship she was never meant to repay. At nineteen she married a riverboat gambler who taught her faro and died of cholera at Cairo in 1853, leaving her his layout and his debts. She paid the debts in a year. She has dealt faro in St. Louis, Denver, Virginia City in Nevada, and since September 1864 in Mordecai Pottinger's Union Saloon in Ninebark, where she rents the corner table for a third of the house's take. Pottinger plays at her bank himself, badly, and owes her eleven hundred dollars. On 6 November, at the foot of the gallows, Jack Tillery named names, and somebody wrote down 'the faro woman at the Union' in a column headed BANISH. Leonie does not yet know that. Pottinger does. (Suggested hook: the warning card under her door on Friday night, 18 November. Leonie is the most direct way for the list to become the players' problem; the GM should ask the player before using it.)
